note: Section 2.1 uses lowercase should for AS-wide uniqueness. The single-positive annotation is appropriate: intentional duplication remains accepted through allow-shared-router-id, while Section 2.2 still rejects zero and internal self identifiers. TestRouterIDClaimConcurrentOnlyOneWins prepares sixteen peers of one AS, validates one shared identifier concurrently, requires exactly one acceptance, requires a routerIDConflictError for every other peer, and verifies the holder and absence of an unrelated claim. Peer.validateOpen and routerIDClaims.claim use the judged AS and serialize claim insertion. TestRFC6286LocalIdentifierUniqueWithinItsAS separately requires exact NOTIFICATION 2/3 and no OpenConfirm for the local identifier from an internal peer. Blanket acceptance and blanket refusal cannot satisfy these assertions. This row credits default advisory uniqueness, not an assertion that explicit operator options have been removed.
